author: Linnaeus, 1758
habitat: 참나무·소나무 등 고목과 노거수가 있는 울창한 숲
summary: 강원도, 경기도, 경상북도, 충청남·북도에 사는 딱다구리로, 수령이 오랜 참나무나 소나무 같은 고목과 노거수가 있는 울창한 숲에서 지낸다. 몸을 곧추세워 나무줄기에 붙은 채 나선을 그리며 올라가 이웃 나무로 옮기고, 부리로 줄기를 두드려 구멍을 파서 곤충 애벌레를 잡아먹는다. 곤충을 주로 먹고 식물 열매도 먹는다. 암수가 함께 땅에서 4~25m 높이의 나무줄기에 구멍을 파 둥지를 만들고 3~5월에 흰 알 3~6개를 낳으며, 국외에서는 스칸디나비아, 프랑스, 스페인, 캄차카반도, 일본에 분포한다.

points.en: glossy dark red forehead to nape (male)
greyish-white bill with black culmen and tip

sexes.male: 이마에서 머리꼭대기를 지나 뒷머리까지 광택 있는 어두운 붉은색이다.

art.subject: Black Woodpecker (Dryocopus martius), adult male as seen in Korean old-growth forests: whole plumage black with a slight gloss and no white anywhere; forehead, crown and nape glossy crimson-red, forming a complete red cap. Bill long, strong and chisel-tipped, pale ivory-grey with a black culmen and tip; pale yellowish-white iris; legs and feet sturdy and grey.
art.pose: clinging upright to a trunk, hammering out a hole with its bill
art.scene: old-growth Korean forest with ancient oaks and pines in spring; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view clinging to a trunk: all-black plumage, glossy crimson-red cap from forehead to nape, pale ivory bill with a black tip, pale eye, sturdy grey legs, tail pressed against the bark
adult female, head close-up in side view: black forehead and crown, red patch only on the hindcrown, pale ivory bill with a black tip
art.build: Very large woodpecker, 45–57cm, about the size of a Large-billed Crow but slimmer, with a slender neck, angular head and long stiff tail used as a prop against the trunk. Bill straight and chisel-tipped, about as long as the head. Legs short and strong, grey, with two toes forward and two back. Flight direct and rather irregular, not deeply undulating, on broad rounded wings.
avoid: Do not paint white on the belly, rump or wings — White-bellied Woodpecker has those; this species is entirely black.
Do not paint a dark bill; it is pale ivory-grey with a black culmen and tip.
Do not paint red on the female's forehead and crown; she has red only on the hindcrown.
Do not give it white face stripes or a pointed crest like a Pileated Woodpecker.
